text:
Elena Park: quick triage for Copperwood private/VPC onboarding - two last-mile blocks: KMS access failing in their CI pipeline and our audit-log forwarder getting TLS alerts from their SIEM. Can we run through checks?

Ravi Desai: saw the CI failure this morning: kms:GenerateDataKey -> AccessDenied. Most often key policy principal mismatch. Did they share the policy?

copperwood-ops: sharing policy snippet in ticket CS-6299: `{\"Version\":\"2012-10-17\",\"Statement\":[{\"Effect\":\"Allow\",\"Principal\":{\"AWS\":\"arn:aws:iam::554433221100:role/cw-ci-role-session\"},\"Action\":[\"kms:Decrypt\",\"kms:GenerateDataKey\"]}]}`

Marta Ruiz: yep that's the session suffix issue. We ask for the role ARN (no session) in the policy. Also request `aws sts get-caller-identity --output text --query Arn` from their CI run to confirm.

Elena Park: asked them to run sts and paste output. Meanwhile infra-bot shows our NAT -> 10.100.4.12:443 TLS alert (handshake failure).

Ravi Desai: question: is their SIEM using client cert auth? If so, we may be hitting cert CN/SAN mismatch or SNI mismatch. Ask them to provide curl -v from their collector and our side.

copperwood-ops: sts output pasted: `arn:aws:sts::554433221100:assumed-role/cw-ci-role/gha-runner-7`. Applying key policy change now to reference `arn:aws:iam::554433221100:role/cw-ci-role`.

Marta Ruiz: good. Also double-check there are no conditional statements on kms:ViaService or aws:SourceAccount that would block cross-account CI.

Elena Park: added runbook reminder to ticket: require "KMS principal exact ARN", "example sts output", and "egress DNS + IP + SG ingress list" up-front. infra-bot confirms runbook https://redwood.internal/runbooks/private-onboard updated.

Ravi Desai: once KMS change is applied, I'll watch the pipeline for GenerateDataKey success. For the TLS issue, please attach `curl -v --cert client.pem --key client.key https://logs.copperwood-sec.internal/health` output from their SIEM and also a `openssl s_client -connect 10.100.4.12:443 -servername logs.copperwood-sec.internal` from our NAT. That will show TLS alerts.

copperwood-ops: attached curl output - shows `SSL: TLSv1.2 alert unknown ca (unknown error)`. They say the cert chain is signed by internal CA.

Marta Ruiz: that suggests our forwarder doesn't trust their CA. Two options: 1) they provide the CA bundle and we add it to the forwarder trust store for this customer (temporary onboarding path); 2) they configure a publicly-signed cert or a mutual TLS endpoint we trust. Note: option 1 requires audit ticket and expiration.

Elena Park: propose offering a temporary CA trust for 72h for onboarding tests, with an audit-approved entry. If they prefer long-term, recommend using a cert from a public CA or using a TLS-terminated proxy.

Ravi Desai: KMS policy rolled; pipeline re-run shows GenerateDataKey succeeded on second attempt. KMS resolved.

infra-bot: Audit reminder: any temporary CA additions must be recorded in CS-6299 and approved by security@redwood. Timestamp 2026-03-22T11:02:00Z.

Marta Ruiz: I'll coordinate security approval for a 72h trust window if Copperwood requests it. Also asked them to confirm removal after onboarding.

copperwood-ops: prefer temporary CA trust for cutover testing this afternoon. signed access window in ticket and uploaded CA bundle.

Elena Park: scheduling 30m pairing at 15:00 UTC to apply trust, run a smoke log flush, and capture tcpdump if needed. Also noting renewal risk: this account is on a 14-day onboarding SLA and we're at day 9; if we hit a blocker >48h escalate to AM.

Ravi Desai: I'll be on the pairing and will tcpdump on NAT if handshake still fails: `sudo tcpdump -n host 10.100.4.12 and port 443 -w /tmp/cw.pcap`

Marta Ruiz: capture feedback item: add a short section in the onboarding checklist about private CA workflows and required artifacts (CA bundle, cert chain, expected CN/SAN). Filing ONB-10044.

Elena Park: thanks team, looping AM if anything extends past 48h. Will update CS-6299 after the 15:00 pairing. :white_check_mark:
